segments.text: Welcome to CardAuction!
It's a game for two players, all about numbers you build with cards.
If you can count to 100, you can play. Let's learn every rule, then how to play in the app.
Players take turns making numbers, and each new number must be a little higher than the last: it's an auction.
The first player who can't make a new bid loses.
CardAuction uses 120 cards.
Most are number cards, each showing one digit, from 0 to 9.
Each number card has a suit with its own color: gold stars, blue diamonds, green clubs, red hearts and black spades.
Here, color and suit mean the same thing. And every card comes in two copies.
The other 20 cards are action cards, marked plus or minus 10.
To make a number, put two number cards side by side: the left one gives the tens, the right one the units.
A 7 and a 3 make 73.
A 0 and a 5 make 05: just five, written with two digits.
To set up, shuffle the cards. The first two number cards turned over make the starting number: here, 47.
Each player gets 13 cards, and 25 go face up in the middle: that's the table.
The other 67 stay face down, out of the game.
Any card you take from the table stays visible to your opponent.
Player 2 starts with one small choice: swap one card from their hand for one on the table, or keep their hand.
Then Player 1 makes the first bid, using exactly one card from the table with cards from their hand.
After that, you take turns. On your turn, you make a bid, then take one card from the table.
Now, the heart of the game. A bid must follow just two rules.
Rule one: count up. Your number must be 1 to 10 steps above the latest bid.
Say the latest bid is 58.
One step: 59.
Two steps: 60.
All the way to ten steps: 68.
Any number from 59 to 68 is fine.
But 58 itself is not: you must go up at least one step. And 69 is too far: that's eleven steps.
Numbers here have only two digits, so after 99 comes 00.
Picture the mileage counter in a car: after 99, it rolls over to 00, and keeps counting: 01, 02, and so on.
CardAuction counts the same way. If the latest bid is 95, count up:
That's ten steps: from 95, you may bid anything from 96 all the way around to 05.
But 94 goes backward, and 06 is eleven steps away.
You can also picture the numbers on a dial, like a clock with 100 marks. You always move forward, 1 to 10 marks, and after 99 the dial keeps going.
So right after 99, the next bid can be anything from 00 to 09.
A small number can top a big one, when you count up past 99 to reach it.
Rule two: your bid needs at least one color that the latest bid doesn't have.
Say the latest bid is 5 of hearts, 8 of spades: 58, in red and black. You'd like to bid 63.
6 of stars and 3 of spades? Yes! The gold star is new.
6 of hearts and 3 of spades? No: red and black are both already in 58.
Your two cards may share a color: 6 of diamonds and 3 of diamonds works, because blue is new.
You may even use both copies of a card: two 6s of diamonds make 66.
Now, the action cards. Just before you bid, an action card moves the latest bid up or down by 10.
Place it beside the latest bid: on the left, it adds 10; on the right, it takes 10 away.
Say the latest bid is 58, and your cards can make 72, but nothing from 59 to 68.
Put an action card on the left: 58 plus 10 is 68.
Count up from 68: 69 to 78. 72 fits!
On the right, 58 minus 10 is 48: you may bid from 49 up to 58. This time, 58 itself is allowed.
Action cards roll over too: 95 plus 10 is 05, so you may bid from 06 to 15.
And 03 minus 10 rolls back to 93: you may bid from 94 around to 03.
The color rule still applies.
After every bid, take one card from the table: a missing number, a new color, or an action card can save you later.
The cards you bid stay on the bid board. When the table is empty, you take nothing.
Remember Player 1's first bid, with exactly one table card?
Say the starting number is 47. The table has a 5 of stars, and you hold a 2 of hearts.
Together they make 52: five steps up, with a new color. Perfect.
The table card can also be an action card, used with two cards from your hand.
The game ends when a player can't make a legal bid on their turn: that player loses.
Say the latest bid is 87. You need a number from 88 to 97, so your tens card must be an 8 or a 9.
With no 8, no 9, and no action card to help, you're stuck, and you lose.
And if Player 1 can't make the first bid, Player 2 wins.
In the app, each turn has a 60-second clock. If it runs out while you must bid, you lose. If it runs out during Player 2's swap, they just keep their hand.
Let's play in the app. Open the CardAuction website: the address is on your screen.
Type your name, then pick a way to play: Quick match, against the next person looking for a game;
Play the AI, with a level and a seat;
or Private game, to invite a friend with a code or a link.
Here's the table: your hand at the bottom, the table cards in the middle, and the bid board with every bid so far.
At the top, your opponent's cards: face down, except the ones they took from the table.
On your turn, tap a card for the tens, then one for the units. The app shows your number and checks it.
If a bid can't work, it tells you why.
For an action card, tap it, then the plus 10 or minus 10 slot beside the latest bid.
Then tap a table card to take, and press Confirm.
With Assist on, the cards that fit a legal move light up.
As Player 2, your first move is the swap: tap a card in your hand and a table card, or keep your hand.
Lost your connection? You have 25 seconds to come back.
At the end, both hands are revealed, and you can ask for a rematch.
And the rules are always one tap away, in English or French.
That's everything! Count up 1 to 10 steps, remember that after 99 comes 00, bring a new color, and use your action cards wisely.
Have fun, and good luck!
